neighbours.label: How much of a resource a population or process needs or consumes (cattle need a lot of feed, an abundance of water for cooling), vs the same subjects without resource demand
fire: Dairy cows drink a huge amount of water every day.
A growing city needs more electricity each year to keep up with demand.
Pigs eat a lot of grain before they are ready for market.
Data centres consume vast quantities of water for cooling.
By 2040, global demand for food is expected to rise sharply.
Elephants must eat hundreds of kilograms of plants daily.
Steel mills use enormous amounts of coal and power.
A hive needs enough honey stored to survive the winter.
quiet: Dairy cows rest in the shade of the barn.
A growing city builds new parks each year.
Pigs roll in the mud to stay cool.
Data centres are often built near large rivers.
By 2040, the old bridge is expected to be replaced.
Elephants live in close family groups.
Steel mills employ thousands of local workers.
A hive swarms when the old queen leaves in spring.

predictions: Statements of resource needs reach 0.2-0.6; same-subject sentences without consumption stay under 0.1.
notes: Card (max 5.75): 'abundance of water', 'multiple doses', 'cows need to eat during the winter', 'a LOT of feed', 'world population expected to grow'.
